maya (ML Eng): Quick sync: we need a synthetic traffic generator that gives apples-to-apples perf curves for kernel-selection experiments + the new batching heuristics. Regression showed ~12% p99 increase after the batching tweak.

evan (runtime): Which regression run? model / seq mix / infra? :eyes:

maya (ML Eng): Regression run id 2026-08-11-kerbench, model=gpt-xl-8k, seq mix=64/512/2048 (60/30/10). Baseline vs batching-v2. I can paste the perf tail logs in a sec.

perf-bot: perf/regression/2026-08-11-kerbench created (run=1876500000) :chart_with_upwards_trend:

jordan (perf): We should standardize the workload before we blame kernels. Proposal: a generator with three modes: steady-state (long warm), microburst (short, high qps bursts), and long-tail spike mode (episodic bursts). Deterministic seeds + replayable bursts so comparisons are stable.

samira (QA): Also need explicit KV cache control: simulate cold / warm / partially-warm states. We must be able to set prefix-reuse ratio and inter-request spacing so KV hit patterns are configurable.

evan (runtime): Agreed. Minimum metrics to capture: per-request token latency, queue_delay_ms, batch_size, kernel_choice, kernel_time_ms, GPU_util%, CPU_spin_ms, KV_hit boolean. Also capture sys-level counters (ctx switches, nvlink).

jordan (perf): Config sketch (portable JSON):
```
{
  "seed": 1234,
  "duration_s": 600,
  "clients": 200,
  "qps_profile": [
    {"t":0, "qps": 50},
    {"t":120, "qps": 300},
    {"t":300, "qps": 1200, "burst": {"rate": 2000, "duration_s": 2, "pattern": "poisson"}}
  ],
  "seq_len_dist": {"64":0.6, "512":0.3, "2048":0.1},
  "kv": {"prefix_reuse_p": 0.7, "keyspace_per_client": 1000, "ttl_s": 120},
  "kernel_probe": {"toggle_policy": ["baseline","batching-v2"], "oscillate_every_s": 60}
}
```

maya (ML Eng): Important: include a "spawned_keyspaces" mode where each synthetic client has an independent keyspace to avoid warmup bias. If we always reuse the same prefix, a new kernel that'll rely on KV will look artificially better.

evan (runtime): Also add a "kv-warmup" phase flag: warm the KV for X minutes with the same distribution, then run the measurement window. For apples-to-apples we must run baseline and candidate back-to-back on the same infra snapshot and run N seeds.

samira (QA): For reporting, let's capture median-of-runs p50/p90/p99 and also per-run variance. Suggest N=5. Use median-of-medians for stability. Export traces as per-token CSV so we can do waterfall attribution: queue wait vs kernel exec vs memory copy.

jordan (perf): We need a kernel-oscillation probe to force comparable batch shapes but flip kernel selection policy. Log emitted events: "kernel_choice", "batch_size", "batch_fill_ms", "queue_delay_ms". That lets us count kernel switches and correlate with tail regression.

maya (ML Eng): Profiling hooks to include: GPU kernel timestamps, CPU callstacks (sampled), NVTX markers around batch boundaries, and a small inline flame for per-token path. Without these we can't tell whether tail is queue formation or kernel slowdown.

evan (runtime): One more gotcha: quantify warmup bias. If candidate has better caching for prefix X, it will show improved p50 during warm-start-only runs. Run a "randomized-keyspace" variant and a "fixed-keyspace" variant and report both.

maya (ML Eng): Invocation example for the harness: `./synth-gen --config configs/kernel_bench.json --out /tmp/run123 --seed 1234 --duration 600 --mode=longtail-spikes`

deploy-bot: deploy/bench-env pinned to infra-snapshot:2026-08-11-5a7c (gpus=8 x a100, kernel=5.12.0, cudnn=8.4)

perf-bot: benchmark finished 1876550300 summary: p50=12ms p90=48ms p99=220ms (tail +11.6% vs baseline) -- full trace: /perf/artifacts/1876550300.zip

samira (QA): Next actions: 1) implement kv modes (spawned/randomized/fixed), 2) add kernel_probe toggle, 3) ensure RNG seeds in config, 4) run N=5 seeds on same snapshot. I'll own validation.

jordan (perf): I'll add the batch-level NVTX markers + an extra counter for kernel_switches.

evan (runtime): I'll wire the kernel_choice logger and add per-token trace hooks.

maya (ML Eng): Great. Let's reconvene after first N=3 runs. If tail persists we'll triage with perf flame graphs. :thumbsup:
